key_insight: Brain age (brain-PAD) captured neurodegeneration-related brain changes across multiple diseases and added information beyond standard global atrophy measures, especially in AD and MS.
clinical_relevance: Brain-PAD may help identify patients with worse current and future cognitive decline across neurodegenerative disorders, supporting its use as a transdiagnostic biomarker alongside routine volumetric MRI measures.
method: Compared patients with controls across AD, FTD, MS, and PD
Benchmarked brain-PAD against brain parenchymal fraction (BPF) for added value
Tested cross-sectional, longitudinal, and voxel-wise structural associations with cognition
evidence_signal: In this transdiagnostic evaluation, brain-PAD distinguished patients from controls in AD, FTD, and MS, correlated with cognition, and predicted later cognitive change in AD, FTD, and MS beyond BPF.
watch_item: The added value was not seen in Parkinson’s disease, so performance may vary by disorder and requires disease-specific validation before broad implementation.
paper_title: The value of brain age as a transdiagnostic biomarker of neurodegeneration
